name: Food Truck Tuesday at Larkin Square
blurb: Buffalo's biggest dinner party returns for its 13th season every Tuesday evening at Larkin Square, featuring a rotating lineup of 20+ regional food trucks and free live music.

name: Buffalo Pride Flag Raising
blurb: The official kick-off to Buffalo Pride Week with the raising of the Pride Flag at City Hall.

name: KeyBank Live at Larkin
blurb: Buffalo's beloved free Wednesday evening concert series in Larkinville runs June through August, featuring local bands alongside food trucks and a full bar.

name: Thursday & Main
blurb: Free weekly outdoor concert series running every Thursday evening at Fountain Plaza, celebrating its 10th anniversary season with a mix of local and national acts.

name: Buffalo Greek Fest
blurb: The 48th Annual Buffalo Greek Fest brings authentic Greek cuisine, pastries, live music, and traditional folk dancing to the Annunciation Greek Orthodox Church.

name: 5th Annual Kick-Off to Buffalo Pride Party
blurb: A community night of music, dancing, drag, food, and photo booth fun benefiting GLYS WNY, Inc., launching Pride Week.

name: M&T First Friday: Pride! at the AKG
blurb: Pride-themed First Friday programming including a Weaving with Pride community art project, drop-in drawing, and a Queering the Collection gallery tour.

name: Pridechella
blurb: An 18+ music-festival drag spectacular billed as seven realms colliding, with headlining queens and DJ MRKUS, kicking off Buffalo Pride weekend.

name: Intersect: A Pride Arts Festival
blurb: A free outdoor Pride arts festival closing Allen Street in the Historic Allentown District with 50+ vendors, live art, queer performers, and an outdoor stage centered around 26 Allen.

name: Buffalo Pride Parade
blurb: The annual Buffalo Pride Parade marching under the theme "Rooted in Pride," stepping off at Elmwood and Forest at 11 a.m. and finishing at Elmwood and Allen.

name: Thursday at Canalside Concert Series
blurb: Free weekly Thursday night concerts at Buffalo's Erie Canal Harbor waterfront, running through late August with diverse regional and national artists.

name: NYS Craft Brewers Festival - Buffalo
blurb: Over 50 New York State breweries pour unique and award-winning beers at Buffalo Canalside, accompanied by live music, food trucks, a keg toss, and a Beer & Wing VIP pairing.

name: Allentown Art Festival
blurb: One of the oldest and largest outdoor art festivals in the country, filling the Allentown Historic Preservation District with hundreds of fine artists and craftspeople each June.

name: Juneteenth Festival of Buffalo
location: Martin Luther King Jr. Park, Buffalo
blurb: The 50th anniversary Juneteenth Festival of Buffalo is one of the nation's longest-running celebrations of African American freedom and heritage, featuring a parade, cultural displays, music, and community programming.

name: Lockport Pride
blurb: A two-day family-friendly Pride event along Main Street in Lockport with over 100 artists, craft and food vendors, and an evening drag performance.

name: Discover Amherst Street Festival
blurb: Free annual neighborhood street festival on Amherst Street between Elmwood and Grant featuring a noon parade, family activities, music, horse-and-buggy rides, and tours of Assumption Church.

name: Roycroft Summer Festival
blurb: An annual arts and crafts festival celebrating the Arts and Crafts movement legacy of the Roycroft Campus, held each final full weekend of June at the Classic Rink in East Aurora.

name: Rainbow City Pride (Niagara Falls)
location: Old Falls Street, Niagara Falls NY
blurb: The 4th Annual Rainbow City Pride on Old Falls Street featuring a DJ, drag performances, drag bingo, belly dancing, and community vendors from 1–6 p.m.

name: Taste of Buffalo
blurb: One of the largest two-day food festivals in the United States, Taste of Buffalo showcases dozens of local restaurants along downtown streets drawing over 400,000 attendees.

name: South Buffalo Porchfest
blurb: A free, family-friendly afternoon festival where dozens of local bands take over porches and lawns across South Buffalo for a sprawling, walkable neighborhood music celebration.

name: East Side Garden Walk
blurb: A self-guided tour of 100+ eclectic private gardens, community plots, and urban farms on Buffalo's East Side, celebrating community beauty and resilience.

name: Canal Fest of the Tonawandas
blurb: The Twin Cities' beloved eight-day community festival along the Historic Erie Barge Canal draws nearly 300,000 visitors with food, live music, arts and crafts, and family events, moving to Gratwick Park for 2026.

name: Galbani Buffalo Italian Heritage Festival
blurb: Celebrating its 50th anniversary, this beloved street festival on Hertel Avenue features authentic Italian food, wine, music, and cultural traditions in the heart of North Buffalo.

name: Cheektowaga Polish American Arts Festival
location: Cheektowaga Town Park, 2600 Harlem Rd, Cheektowaga
blurb: The 46th annual Polish American Arts Festival offers free admission to celebrate Polish heritage through food, traditional music, dance groups, crafts, and cultural exhibits at Cheektowaga Town Park.

name: Queen City Jazz Festival
location: Buffalo & Erie County Central Library, Downtown Buffalo
blurb: The 22nd annual free outdoor jazz festival hosted by the Historic Colored Musicians Club, featuring live performances from regional and national jazz artists.

name: Garden Walk Buffalo
blurb: America's largest free garden tour, featuring more than 300 gardens across Buffalo neighborhoods in a self-guided weekend walk always held the last full weekend of July.

name: Cobblestone Live Music & Arts Festival
blurb: A two-day multi-stage outdoor music festival in Buffalo's historic Cobblestone District featuring indie, funk, electronic, and acoustic acts across five stages.

name: Jack Craft Fair
blurb: Buffalo's premier alternative arts festival at Larkin Square, showcasing 100+ local and independent makers with handmade goods, art, and community vendors.

name: Buffalo Irish Festival
blurb: The Buffalo Irish Festival brings two days of live Irish music, dance performances, cultural workshops on literature and language, and a Kids Zone to River Fest Park on the waterfront.

name: Lewiston Art Festival
blurb: A juried outdoor art festival drawing 200+ artists to Center Street in the historic Village of Lewiston, featuring a Chalk Walk competition, Indigenous Market, and live performances.

name: Puerto Rican & Hispanic Day Parade and Festival
location: Niagara Square / Niagara Street (Avenida San Juan), Buffalo
blurb: The 24th Annual Puerto Rican and Hispanic Day Parade marches down Avenida San Juan to Niagara Square, followed by a free outdoor concert celebrating the Latino heritage of Western New York.

name: National Buffalo Wing Festival
blurb: The 25th Annual National Buffalo Wing Festival moves to Sahlen Field for the weekend before Labor Day, offering unlimited wing samples from 20+ vendors alongside the U.S. Chicken Wing Eating Championship.

name: Buffalo Jazz Festival
blurb: The 5th annual Labor Day Sunday jazz festival headlined by Brazilian-style jazz ensemble Três Mais and Grammy-nominated vocalist Karrin Allyson.

name: Music is Art Festival
blurb: A free all-day celebration of Buffalo's music scene featuring over 200 bands across 20 stages, DJs, performance art, and family programming at the Outer Harbor.

name: Borderland Music and Arts Festival
location: Knox Farm State Park, East Aurora
blurb: A three-day grassroots camping music festival at Knox Farm State Park featuring national headliners (Jack White, Alabama Shakes, Lord Huron) alongside indie, folk, and Americana acts.

name: Shop, Rock & Stroll — Hertel Avenue End-of-Summer Edition
blurb: The Hertel Business Association's recurring last-Friday-of-the-month street activation turns the avenue into an open-air party with live music, boutique shopping, and dining through September.
